MiniCPM-2B-SFT now uses the complete learned checkpoint count, including shared embeddings once; obsolete non-embedding scope is removed.

The February, March and April 2024 rotation resolves the exact MiniCPM DPO, DeepSeek Math/MoE and CodeQwen inventory gaps. DeepSeekMoE was released in January and DeepSeekMath in February, so neither is labeled a March release.

Resolved historical gap strings are removed explicitly; unrelated gaps and reviewed-with-gaps status remain. New exact-checkpoint MiniCPM license questions are retained in February and the pending queue.

Eight March 2025 Sarashina releases and legacy Sarashina mini retain month precision; technical-article dates and planned API dates do not establish exact first access. The gated Sarashina2.2 Vision count is public checkpoint metadata, not an independent header audit; context remains null.

North Micro Vision includes its full language and vision checkpoint. Supported text context remains nominal 128K with only 8K validated for multimodal input; the larger configured position limit is not promoted to supported context.

Nemotron 3.5 Parse includes the vision encoder, adapter, language decoder and MTP head; persistent normalization and summary-index buffers are excluded. MiniCPM OCR keeps its optional dependent DSpark head separate.

Parse v5.0 remains pending because its distinct trained identity versus North Micro Vision Instruct is unresolved. API naming, different rounded parameter labels and deployment packaging do not establish a separate checkpoint.
The independently pretrained Diffusion Conveyer release is included with an author-reported nominal count; first release date and exact released-checkpoint context remain unknown.
QwenPaw month precision is preserved, and the October 9B RL-step109 provenance question remains open. Publisher migrations and repository timestamps are not treated as release dates.
Source metadata refreshes for IFM K2 Horizon 0.9B and two Liquid LFM2.5 checkpoints have unchanged weight identities; no catalog correction is invented for those updates.
Gemini 4 Carbon, MAI-Base-2 and Hy4 general availability remain unverified. Dessa remains limited; benchmark appearances, waitlists and future rollout language are not first-access evidence.

Hugging Face discovery streams reached their overlap boundaries or exhausted pagination. ModelScope stopped at the public 3000-row cap; Artificial Analysis credentials were unavailable and manual AA/Arena/publisher checks are partial.
Queue updates use exact candidate identifiers and explicit canonical identities. References to related checkpoints do not close separate unresolved research questions.

Replay validation exposed and fixed two discovery failures: collector IDs were wrapped as research IDs, and a manually unresolved identity question could close automatically because it cited a related model. Explicit null identity decisions and original collector evidence now survive replay.
